---
applyTo: "app/decorators/**/*.rb,app/controllers/**/*.rb,app/views/**/*,app/helpers/**/*.rb,spec/decorators/**/*.rb,spec/support/**/*.rb"
---

# Draper

- Use a decorator method for presentation logic about one record, not a helper, e.g. `post.published_on` in `PostDecorator` instead of `post_published_on(post)` in `PostsHelper`.
- Keep helpers for general view elements that are not about one record, e.g. `success_badge` or `date_tag`. Call those helpers from the decorator through `h`, e.g. `h.date_tag(object.published_at)` in `PostDecorator`.
- Keep decorator methods simple: return a formatted value, a link, or a small element built with a helper, e.g. `status_badge` in `PostDecorator`. Never render a component or a partial from a decorator, e.g. `h.render(Posts::CardComponent.new(post: object))`. Render it in the view instead.
- Only change a decorator method's output based on the record's state or a record passed in its context, e.g. `object.published?` in `PostDecorator#status_badge`. Never base it on the request, e.g. the current user, the params or a permission check. The `can_` permission checks are the only exception.
- When a decorator method shows a value that is not known, prefer to return `h.unknown_value_tag`, or the app's own alternative if it already shows missing values another way, over `nil`, e.g. in `PostDecorator#published_on` when `object.published_at` is `nil`.
- Name a decorator after its model and inherit from `ApplicationDecorator`, e.g. `class PostDecorator < ApplicationDecorator` in `app/decorators/post_decorator.rb`.
- Lay out a decorator in groups, each under a `### Name ###` comment, in this order: the `delegate` line and the methods that format attributes, with no heading; then `### Links ###` for every method that returns a link to the record, e.g. `link` and `edit_link`; then groups for the app's own elements, e.g. `### Badges ###` with `status_badge`; then one group for each association, named after it, e.g. `### Comments ###` with `decorates_association :comments` and its delegates; then `### Policy ###` last for the permission checks, e.g. `delegate :publish?, to: :policy, prefix: :can`.
- Never decorate an instance variable in a controller. Assign the plain record and decorate it with `decorates_assigned`, e.g. `decorates_assigned :post` in `PostsController` with `@post = Post.find(params[:id])`, then call `post` instead of `@post` in the view.
- Avoid `delegate_all`, except in legacy code that already relies on it. Delegate each model method the view reads by name, and read the model through `object` inside the decorator, e.g. `delegate :title` and `object.published_at` in `PostDecorator`.
- In a decorator, only delegate a model method when the view shows its value as it is, e.g. `delegate :title`. When a value needs consistent formatting, e.g. a date or a status, write a decorator method for it instead of delegating the attribute, e.g. `published_on` instead of `delegate :published_at`.
- Pass a decorator with the `with:` argument when a view needs a specific decorator, e.g. `decorates_assigned :post, with: Posts::SummaryDecorator`.
- Never call `decorate` in a view or a helper, e.g. `@post.decorate` in `app/views/posts/show.html.erb` or `PostDecorator.new(post)` in `PostsHelper`. Add a `decorates_assigned` to the controller instead.
- Only use Draper for HTML responses. Never use `decorates_assigned` or a decorator in an API endpoint that returns another format, e.g. JSON from `Api::V1::PostsController`.
- Never use Draper in mailers. Never add `decorates_assigned` to a mailer, e.g. `PostMailer`. In mailer templates, use the plain record with helpers and `_url` helpers for links, e.g. `<%= link_to @post.title, post_url(@post) %>` and `<%= date_tag(@post.published_at) %>` in `app/views/post_mailer/published.html.erb`.
- When a decorator needs a record it cannot reach from its own record, pass it with the `context:` option, and pass the parent's decorated helper method, e.g. `decorates_assigned :tag` (usually in `Tags::BaseController`) and `decorates_assigned :posts, context: ->(c) { { tag: c.tag } }` in `Tags::PostsController` for `GET /tags/:tag_id/posts`, then read it through a private method that calls `fetch`, e.g. `def tag = context.fetch(:tag)` in `PostDecorator`, used as `h.tag_post_path(tag, object)` in `PostDecorator#tag_post_link`. Only pass records in the context, never the current user, the params or other request state.
- Decorate a required association in the decorator with `decorates_association`, e.g. `decorates_association :post` in `CommentDecorator`.
- Never reach through an association in a view, e.g. `comment.post.published_on`. Delegate the methods the view needs to the decorated association with a prefix, e.g. `delegate :title, :published_on, to: :post, prefix: true` in `CommentDecorator`, then call `comment.post_published_on`.
- For an optional association, write the association method yourself instead of `decorates_association`, fall back to a `NilDecorator` when the record is `nil`, and memoise the result, e.g. `def author = @author ||= object.author&.decorate || NilDecorator.for(User)` in `PostDecorator`, then `delegate :name, to: :author, prefix: true`.
- Build `NilDecorator.for(klass)` in `app/decorators/nil_decorator.rb` as a stand-in for the decorator of `klass`, e.g. `NilDecorator.for(User)` for `UserDecorator`. Return `false` for every `can_` method ending in `?` that `klass.new.decorate` responds to, e.g. `can_update?`, and `h.unknown_value_tag` for every other method it responds to. Raise `NoMethodError` for a method it does not respond to, and return `false` from `present?`, `true` from `blank?` and `nil` from `presence`.
- Only add `decorates_association` for a `has_many` association when a view uses the whole association, e.g. `decorates_association :comments` in `PostDecorator`. Put it in the association's group.
- When a view needs a scoped part of an association, add a scoped association to the model and decorate it with `decorates_association`, e.g. `has_many :approved_comments, -> { approved }, class_name: "Comment"` in `Post` and `decorates_association :approved_comments` in `PostDecorator`. Never build the scope in the decorator, e.g. `object.comments.approved`. Put it in the association's group.
- Decorate a collection with `decorates_assigned`, and assign the plain relation, e.g. `decorates_assigned :posts` in `PostsController` with `@posts = Post.all`, then call `posts` in the view.
- Handle an empty collection in the view, e.g. `<% if posts.empty? %>` in `app/views/posts/index.html.erb`, not in a decorator.
- Only write a collection decorator when the view needs a summary value from the whole collection, or the list is paginated. Name it after the plural of the model, inherit from `Draper::CollectionDecorator`, and pass it with `with:`, e.g. `CommentsDecorator#last_comment_at` in `app/decorators/comments_decorator.rb` with `decorates_assigned :comments, with: CommentsDecorator` in `Posts::CommentsController`.
- For a paginated collection, write one concern for each paginator that delegates the paginator's methods to the collection, named after the paginator, and include it in the collection decorator, e.g. `KaminariPagination` in `app/decorators/concerns/kaminari_pagination.rb` with `delegate :current_page, :total_pages, :limit_value, :total_count, :offset_value, :last_page?`, included in `PostsDecorator`.
- With Pundit, build the policy in `ApplicationDecorator` from the view's `policy` helper with `object`, memoise it, and keep the method private, e.g. `def policy = @policy ||= h.policy(object)` under `private`. Never let a view reach through it, e.g. `post.policy.update?`.
- In `ApplicationDecorator`, under a `### Policy ###` comment, delegate the standard Rails action checks to the policy with a `can` prefix, e.g. `delegate :index?, :show?, :new?, :create?, :edit?, :update?, :destroy?, to: :policy, prefix: :can`. Views then call `post.can_update?`, never `post.update?`.
- Delegate a custom action check in the model's own decorator, under its `### Policy ###` comment, with the same `can` prefix, e.g. `delegate :publish?, to: :policy, prefix: :can` in `PostDecorator` for `PostPolicy#publish?`. Views then call `post.can_publish?`.
- When an action the user may do would still fail right now, override its `can_` check in the model's decorator and call the policy first, e.g. `def can_destroy? = super && object.comments.none?` in `PostDecorator` when `Post` has `has_many :comments, dependent: :restrict_with_error`. For a custom action, define the method in place of its `delegate`, e.g. `policy.publish? && ...`. Only add business rules, e.g. a post with comments can't be deleted. Put rules about who may do it in the policy.
- Never make another decorator method depend on a permission, e.g. `edit_link` returning `nil` unless `can_update?`. Let the view decide, e.g. `<% if post.can_update? %><%= post.edit_link %><% end %>`. When the view shows an alternative, add a method for it next to the link and let the view choose, e.g. `PostDecorator#disabled_link` returning `h.tag.span(object.title, aria: { disabled: true })`, with `post.can_show? ? post.link : post.disabled_link` in the view.
- Write a decorator spec in `spec/decorators` for each decorator, with a `describe` block for each method and an example for each path through it, e.g. `it "returns the date it was published"` and `it "returns the unknown value tag for a draft"` for `PostDecorator#published_on`.
- In decorator specs, build the record being decorated with an `instance_double` on its own line, stubbing only the values the method reads, then decorate it on the next line, e.g. `post = instance_double(Post, published_at: nil)` and `decorator = PostDecorator.new(post)`. Use a factory only when an `instance_double` can't stand in for the record.
- In decorator specs, when you need a factory, use `build_stubbed`, e.g. `post = build_stubbed(:post, title: "Hello")` for a method that calls `h.link_to(object.title, object)`. Use `create` only when the method needs the record in the database, e.g. when it runs a query.
- In decorator specs, check an element built with a helper with the helper's matcher, e.g. `expect(decorator.published_on).to have_unknown_value_tag`. Never compare it with markup or the helper's output, e.g. `eq(helpers.unknown_value_tag)`. Include each helper's matcher module for `type: :decorator`, e.g. `config.include UnknownValuesSpecHelpers, type: :decorator` in `spec/support/unknown_values_spec_helpers.rb`.
- In decorator specs, test a method that reads its context by building the record in the example, decorated the same way the controller passes it, and passing it in the decorator's context, e.g. `tag = TagDecorator.new(instance_double(Tag, to_param: "2"))` and `described_class.new(post, context: { tag: tag })` in `it "links to the post under the tag"` for `PostDecorator#tag_post_link`.
- Spec each `can_` method you override, with an example for each path, e.g. `it "allows it when the policy allows it and the post has no comments"`, `it "forbids it when the policy forbids it"` and `it "forbids it when the post has comments"` for `PostDecorator#can_destroy?`. Do not spec the plain `can_` delegates.
- In decorator specs, stub the policy in each example that needs it, not at the top of the spec, with an `instance_double` of the policy class returned from `helpers.policy`, e.g. `allow(helpers).to receive(:policy).with(post).and_return(instance_double(PostPolicy, destroy?: true))`.
